sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No.5399/2025, which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.1 Rajendra @ Raju S/o Halke Choudhary.

This appeal is filed being aggrieved of judgment dated 09/11/2024 passed by the IInd Additional Sessions Judge Gadarwara, District Narsinghpur in Sessions Case No.27/2022 convicting the appellant No.1 for offences punishable under Section 366-A of I.P.C. and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for five years and fine of Rs. 1000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for one month,
Section 363 of I.P.C. and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for three years and fine of Rs. 500/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for fifteen days, Section 5(1)/6 R/w Sect. 16/17 of POCSO Act and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for twenty years and fine of Rs. 2000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for two months, Section 3/4 R/w sub sect. (2) R/w Sect. 16/17 of POCSO Act and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for twenty years and fine of Rs. 2000/- with default stipulation of additional R.I. for two months, Section 376 (2)(N)(109) of I.P.C. and Section 376(3)(109) of I.P.C.
2 CRA-13024-2024 It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the main allegation is on Lal Shahab.

entities.text: IInd Additional Sessions Judge Gadarwara, District Narsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present appellant Rajendra @ Raju has been falsely implicated.
The allegation on Rajendra @ Raju helping co- accused Lal Shahab was with abduction of prosecutrix is not made out.

Lal Shahab was already knowing the prosecutrix and, therefore, the prosecutrix admittedly came out on receiving the phone call of Lal Shahab on the mobile number of her father and,
therefore, the story of prosecution against present appellant Rajendra @ Raju appears to be exaggerated.
There are good chances of success.
The appeal will take time for its conclusion.

Hence,
prayer is made to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and release him on bail.
Learned Government Advocate, on the other hand, opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant No.1 Rajendra @ Raju and to release him on bail.

It is directed that on depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 20.8.2025 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant no.1 Rajendra @ Raju shall remain suspended and he be released on bail till final disposal of 3 CRA-13024-2024 this appeal.
Thus, I.A. No.5399/2025 is allowed and disposed of.
